question.text: If $\int \frac{3 x+1}{(x-3)(x-5)} d x=\int \frac{-5}{(x-3)} d x+\int \frac{B}{(x-5)} d x$ then the value of $B$ is

solution.text:
We have,

$\begin{array}{l}

\frac{3 x+1}{(x-3)(x-5)}=\frac{-5}{x-3}+\frac{\mathrm{B}}{x-5} \\

3 x+1=-5(x-5)+\mathrm{B}(x-3) \\

\text { Put } x=5 \\

3(5)+1=\mathrm{B}(5-3) \\

16=2 \mathrm{~B} \text { or } \mathrm{B}=8

\end{array}$
